title: FP8 RNG-seed intermittent NaNs - investigation notes
body:
Quick context: intermittent NaNs crop up in hosted inference traces when we enable FP8 for decoding. They do not always reproduce; seeding the process sometimes avoids the failure. This note is my working log of commands, small repros, environment permutations, hypotheses, and next steps.

Symptoms observed:
- Production logs show spurts of NaN logits during autoregressive decoding for long prompts (sequence length ~1024).
- Errors observed in two flavors: (1) immediate NaN in the softmax input (logits) and (2) NaN appears after a KV cache write -> subsequent attention returns NaN.
- Failures are bursty: many requests succeed, then a small fraction fail with NaN.

Environment snapshot (where failures reported):
- Serving runtime: release-2025-02-28 (custom kernel selection enabled)
- Model: open-llm-7b-fp8 (per-model quant config: mantissa=6, exp_biasAdjusted=true)
- Torch: 2.2.0+cu121, CUDA driver: 530.41, cudnn: 9.0.2
- HW: NVIDIA A100 80GB (multi-tenant on Dedicated pool)

Immediate reproducibility attempts (local bench):
1) Baseline: run decoder with deterministic seed (torch.manual_seed(42))
   ./bench_decode.sh 
   OUTPUT: no NaNs after 1000 runs

2) Randomized seeds loop (no seed set):
   for i in {1..200}; do TORCH_SEED=$RANDOM ./bench_decode.sh || echo "FAIL $i" >> fails.log; done
   OUTPUT: ~2 fails in 200 (intermittent) -> consistent with production rate

3) Re-run failing seed value captured from logs: TORCH_SEED=17429 ./bench_decode.sh
   OUTPUT: reproduces NaN 100% of the time for seed 17429

4) Re-run same seed but disable FP8 quant path (fall back to BF16 path):
   set QUANT_MODE=bf16 TORCH_SEED=17429 ./bench_decode.sh
   OUTPUT: no NaN (immediately suggests FP8-specific path)

5) Run with deterministic CuDNN algorithms: TORCH_USE_CUDNN_REPLAY=1 TORCH_BACKEND_CUDNN_DETERMINISTIC=1 TORCH_SEED=17429 ./bench_decode.sh
   OUTPUT: sometimes still NaN (makes non-deterministic kernel choice less likely but not ruled out)

6) Run under asan / address sanitizer instrumented native kernel: rebuild serving runtime with -fsanitize=address (slow) -> crash not always triggered, but when it does it points to fused-gemm-cu kernel near quant-dequant transition.

Key logs (redacted):
- Decoder step 427: logits[0,512] = NaN, upstream attention scores contain NaN
- Stack snippet: at fused_gemm_kernel.cu:line 412 -> quant_dequant.cu:87 -> kv_cache_write.cu:152
- Runtime message: WARNING: FP8 scale overflow detected, applying clamp -> later still NaN

Commands & quick helpers I used:
- bench_decode.sh (local harness):
  #!/bin/bash
  export MODEL=./models/open-llm-7b-fp8
  export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
  python -u ./tools/decode_repro.py --model $MODEL --max-tokens 512 --batch 1

- Reproducer snippet (decode_repro.py): small script that loads quantized model and runs autoregressive sampling with top_k=40, temperature=0.8, uses builtin sampling.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) RNG -> quant rounding interaction: specific RNG states produce activation distributions that trigger FP8 exponent/scale overflow during quantize step, leading to Inf/NaN during subsequent operations. Evidence: seed 17429 reproducible, disabling FP8 removes failure.
2) KV-cache accumulation: repeated small rounding errors in quant/dequant cause cached keys/values to slowly drift toward large magnitudes for some layers, eventually overflowing FP8 dynamic range. Evidence: NaNs sometimes only after many decode steps; stack points to kv_cache_write.
3) Kernel bug in fused GEMM + FP8 path: some code path does not apply correct scaling/clamping, producing out-of-range values. Evidence: asan points to fused kernel; intermittent reproducibility suggests memory aliasing or uninitialized read in optimized kernel.
4) Per-device thermal/ASync DMA race: improbable but observed in other releases; kernel non-determinism under load could manifest as bursty NaNs.

What I tried to triage differences between hypotheses:
- Seed bisection: run with seed range +/- neighborhood of failing seed (17420-17440) -> only a small subset fails -> supports RNG-specific distribution effect rather than kernel memory corruption across all seeds.
- Layer-level isolation: instrumented model to run quantization only on a single attention layer (layer 8) while others run bf16 -> reproducer still fails when layer 8 is in fp8, points to layer-local sensitivity.
- Reduce sequence length: truncating to 256 tokens reduces failure rate by ~80% (points to accumulation effect).
- Zero-out KV cache between tokens (simulate no accumulation): dramatically reduces failures -> supports accumulation hypothesis.
- Increase mantissa bits (if supported): using mantissa=7 reduces failure rate -> indicates insufficient dynamic range/precision.

Quick patches/proposals to test in staging (can be A/B tested in Dedicated pool):
- Patch A: Add aggressive clamping after quantize step and early NaN check (return fallback to bf16 on detect). Low cost, masking fix.
- Patch B: Force per-layer dynamic scaling re-estimation on first N tokens to avoid bad initial scale. Medium cost.
- Patch C: Disable fused-gemm heuristic for FP8 on known sensitive layers and fallback to safer kernels. Higher cost but targeted.

Repro recipe to hand to SRE / kernel team:
1) Use docker image: redwood/serve-debug:2025-03-05
2) Run: TORCH_SEED=17429 QUANT_PROFILE=1 ./bench_decode.sh 2>&1 | tee seed17429.log
3) Attach GPU traces: nvprof --profile-from-start off -- sample 1 (or nsight per kernel)
4) If reproduces, record kernel name from nvprof and capture ptx of the fused kernel.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we extract exact quantization scale/amax history per step for the failing run? Implement logging of per-layer amax to S3 for one failing request.
- Is there an upstream pytorch/cuda kernel mismatch? Try reproducing with torch 2.1 and 2.3 nightly to bracket behavior.
- Validate if FP8 exponent bias adjustment (model-level flag) interacts badly with our implementation; toggle exp_biasAdjusted to false to test.
- Ask kernels team to run valgrind-like memory sanitizer across fused kernels under randomized seeds.

Action items (who/when):
- Maya: add per-layer amax logging to bench harness (by EOD)
- Alex: run deterministic kernel builds (-O0) and report whether failing seed still NaN (2 days)
- Sofia: prepare canary with Patch A in Dedicated pool (sandbox) and collect telemetry (1 week)

Notes / miscellany:
- Observed one oddity: when we set TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 the failure rate increases slightly. Could be exposing uninitialized memory.
- Add unit test: small synthetic model (2-layer attention-only) with FP8 quant path + seed loop to surface this under CI nightly.

If anyone else runs into this, drop failing seed values + short prompt + model-checksum into this doc so we can build a seed bank to analyze distribution of bad seeds.

2025-03-07T14:02:11Z DEBUG layer=8 quant amax=3.2e+02 scale=0.003125

References and related tickets:
- INF-4732 (prod spike on hosted API)
- GH PR 1823 (early attempt at clamping in quant path)
- internal issue: confluence://internal/qa/fp8-nan-hypotheses (frag notes)

End of scratchpad.

(If you copy/run anything from this doc, double-check the paths and model names — this is a personal working note, not an official runbook.)
